description: Component for ingesting Facebook Ads data using dlt - returns DataFrames.
summary: Ingest Facebook Ads campaign, ad set, ad, creative, lead, and performance data.

asset_name.label: Asset Name
asset_name.description: Name of the asset that will hold the Facebook Ads data

account_id.label: Account Id
account_id.description: Facebook Ads Account ID (format: act_123456789). Find in Ads Manager URL. Required unless resource_key is set.

access_token.label: Access Token
access_token.description: Facebook Access Token with ads_read and lead_retrieval permissions. Use ${FACEBOOK_ACCESS_TOKEN} for env vars. Required unless resource_key is set.

app_id.label: App Id
app_id.description: Facebook App ID (optional, for long-lived tokens)

app_secret.label: App Secret
app_secret.description: Facebook App Secret (optional, for long-lived tokens)

resource_key.label: Resource Key
resource_key.description: Optional resource key registered by a FacebookAdsResourceComponent. When set, credentials (account_id, access_token, app_id, app_secret) are read from that resource at run time instead of the fields above.

resources.label: Resources
resources.description: Comma-separated list of resources to extract: campaigns, ad_sets, ads, creatives, ad_leads, insights

initial_load_past_days.label: Initial Load Past Days
initial_load_past_days.description: Number of days of historical data to load

ad_states.label: Ad States
ad_states.description: Comma-separated ad states to extract: ACTIVE, PAUSED, DELETED, ARCHIVED, DISAPPROVED, etc.

insights_fields.label: Insights Fields
insights_fields.description: Comma-separated list of insights fields to extract (leave empty for defaults)

insights_breakdown.label: Insights Breakdown
insights_breakdown.description: Insights breakdown dimension: age, gender, country, region, platform, device_platform

time_increment_days.label: Time Increment Days
time_increment_days.description: Time increment for insights reports in days (1 = daily, 7 = weekly)

owners.label: Owners
owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.

asset_tags.label: Asset Tags
asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.

kinds.label: Kinds
kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.

freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)
freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.

freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule
freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).

include_preview_metadata.label: Include Preview Metadata
include_preview_metadata.description: Include sample data preview in metadata

preview_rows.label: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: How many rows to include in the preview. Large tables (>10× this number) are sampled randomly.

destination.label: Destination
destination.description: dlt destination identifier (e.g. 'snowflake', 'bigquery', 'postgres', 'redshift', 'filesystem', 'duckdb', 'databricks', 'athena', 'clickhouse', 'mssql', 'motherduck'). Leave empty for in-memory DuckDB → DataFrame mode.

deps.label: Deps
deps.description: Upstream asset keys this asset depends on (e.g. ['raw_orders', 'schema/asset'])

dataset_name.description: Target dataset/schema in the destination. Defaults to the asset name.
dataset_name.label: Dataset Name

persist_only.description: If True with destination set: emit a MaterializeResult and skip DataFrame return. If False: query the destination back into a DataFrame (only meaningful for SQL destinations — non-SQL destinations always emit MaterializeResult).
persist_only.label: Persist Only

destination_credentials_url.description: Inline connection string passed to dlt's destination factory. Useful when one Dagster project ingests into multiple accounts of the same destination type. If unset, dlt resolves credentials from env vars — see ../DESTINATIONS.md.
destination_credentials_url.label: Destination Credentials Url

fields.name: port
fields.label: Port
fields.description: Native TCP port (not the HTTP interface port)

fields.name: encrypt
fields.label: Encrypt
fields.description: 'yes' to require SSL (e.g. Azure SQL); 'no' for a local unencrypted instance

fields.name: database
fields.label: Database
fields.description: Defaults to 'my_db' on MotherDuck's side if left blank

bigquery.description: Paste the full GCP service-account key JSON (GCP Console -> IAM & Admin -> Service Accounts -> your account -> Keys -> Add Key -> JSON). Used verbatim -- dlt's GcpServiceAccountCredentials parses a raw JSON string directly, so no connection-string assembly happens here.

destination_credentials_env_var.description: Alternative to destination_credentials_url: name of an env var holding the connection string. Resolved at run-time.
destination_credentials_env_var.label: Destination Credentials Env Var

bucket_url.label: Bucket Url
bucket_url.description: Bucket/path URL for filesystem-shaped storage (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/path', 'gs://my-bucket/path', 'az://my-container/path', or 'file:///local/path'). Required when destination='filesystem' (the final write target). Also used as the staging area when destination='databricks' or 'athena', both of which require an intermediate filesystem stage before the warehouse-side load -- dlt resolves the bucket's credentials from the destination-appropriate standard environment variables (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) unless destination_credentials_url/destination_credentials_env_var is set.

athena_query_result_bucket.label: Athena Query Result Bucket
athena_query_result_bucket.description: Optional S3 path where Athena writes query results (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/results/'). Only used when destination='athena'. May be omitted to use Athena-managed query results instead.

partition_type.description: Partition type: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly', or None for unpartitioned. With a partition type set, the partition key is exposed via context.partition_key for use in filtering / templating.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_start.description: Partition start date in ISO format, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required when partition_type is set.
partition_start.label: Partition Start

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

column_lineage.label: Column Lineage
column_lineage.description: Column-level lineage, emitted as `dagster/column_lineage` metadata on every materialization: {output column: [upstream columns]}, e.g. {'revenue': ['price', 'quantity']}. The upstream asset is `upstream_asset_key`, or the only entry of `deps`; with several upstream assets, name each column '<asset_key>:<column>'. Ignored with a warning when no upstream asset can be resolved.

partition_date_column.description: Column used to filter the upstream DataFrame to the current date partition key.
partition_date_column.label: Partition Date Column

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme,globex,initech'.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

partition_static_dim.description: Dimension name for the static axis in multi-partitioning, e.g. 'customer'.
partition_static_dim.label: Partition Static Dim

partition_static_column.description: Column used to filter the upstream DataFrame to the current static partition value.
partition_static_column.label: Partition Static Column

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill execution strategy for a partitioned asset. 'single_run' materializes an entire backfill range in one run: the full dataset is fetched once (as always) and then filtered down to the whole range via Partition Date Column/Partition Static Column (same mechanism as a normal tick, just spanning more rows). 'multi_run' launches one run per partition (optionally capped via Backfill Max Partitions Per Run). Leave empty for Dagster's default (one run per partition, uncapped). Ignored when Partition Type is not set. Requires a partition-range-aware IO manager (e.g. a DB-table IO manager with partition_expr set) -- a generic filesystem/default IO manager cannot persist a single_run output spanning multiple partitions and will raise a clear error at materialization time.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For Backfill Policy = 'multi_run' only: maximum partitions materialized per run. Leave empty for Dagster's default (1).

partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions
partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

asset_shape.label: Asset Shape
asset_shape.description: 'single' (default, matches every other multi-resource ingestion component in this repo): one asset, keyed `asset_name`, covering every resource in `resources` as a single unit -- rows from every resource (including 'insights', loaded via a separate dlt source) are unioned into one returned DataFrame tagged by a `_resource_type` column. 'multi_asset': each resource in `resources` is instead its own independently-materializable asset, keyed `{asset_name}_{resource}` -- select just the resource(s) you want; materializing several together still batches them through one shared dlt pipeline (one run per underlying source, standard vs insights -- one Dagster step overall), not parallel per-resource execution. Opt into 'multi_asset' when you want to select/retry/schedule individual resources separately.

table_name_map.label: Table Name Map
table_name_map.description: Override the destination table name for specific Facebook Ads resources, e.g. {'insights': 'raw_insights'}. Keys must match individual resource names parsed out of `resources` (not the raw comma-separated string). dlt otherwise names each destination table after its resource. Resources in `resources` that aren't listed here keep their resource name as-is. Every key must also appear in `resources`.

hash_columns.label: Hash Columns
hash_columns.description: Column names to pseudonymize (salted SHA-256, hex-encoded) before the data reaches the destination -- same deterministic-hashing pattern dlt's own docs recommend for PII (https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/customising-pipelines/pseudonymizing_columns). A column missing from a given resource's rows is skipped, not an error. Requires hash_salt or hash_salt_env_var.

hash_salt.label: Hash Salt
hash_salt.description: Salt for hash_columns. Required (this or hash_salt_env_var) when hash_columns is set -- a hardcoded/shared salt would let the hash be reversed by dictionary attack on common values. Use "{{ env.VAR_NAME }}" for the inline form. Keep it stable across runs: changing it changes every hash.

hash_salt_env_var.label: Hash Salt Env Var
hash_salt_env_var.description: Alternative to hash_salt: name of an env var holding the salt. Resolved at run-time.

name: Facebook Ads Ingestion
